observations: Photo 0: An orange gas cylinder wrapped in black protective netting, standing outdoors in a market setting with pedestrians and umbrellas in the background.
Photo 0: A brass valve/regulator fitting is visible at the top, appearing shiny.
Photo 0: A dark logo/mark is printed on the cylinder body but is too stylized/small to read a brand name.
Photo 1: Top-down view into the cylinder collar showing the brass valve fitting at the center.
Photo 1: Handwritten marker text 'MX' is visible on the cylinder shoulder - appears to be a chalk/marker tally mark, not a brand or certification stamp.
No visible capacity stamp (e.g. '12kg'), manufacture date, or test certification sticker/stamp is legible in either photo.
No test certificate, pressure gauge reading, or leak-test documentation is shown.
Seller's new reply is text only, restating prior claims; no new photo or video was provided.

claims.evidence: No capacity stamp or country-of-origin marking is legible in photo 0 or photo 1; size is only inferable visually, not confirmed.
No certificate, inspection sticker, or stamped test date visible in either photo; seller's verbal reassurance ('I tested it myself yesterday') is not photographic proof.
No leak test (soap-bubble test, pressure gauge, or video) shown in photos or in the new message.
Photo 1 shows a clean brass valve, consistent with new but not proof of recent replacement; no new evidence given.

risks.risk: Actual cylinder capacity may differ from claimed 12kg.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the stamped capacity marking on the cylinder collar/neck.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified size, using visual estimate only

risks.risk: Cylinder may not actually hold pressure / may leak.
risks.proof: Video of a soap-bubble leak test or a filled pressure gauge reading.

risks.risk: No safety/inspection certification visible, cylinder could be past its safety retest date or of unknown age.
risks.proof: Photo of the stamped manufacture/test date on the collar, or the physical certificate.

risks.risk: Internal corrosion or damage not visible from outside.
risks.proof: Photo/video of interior via valve removed, or a recent hydrostatic test report.

risks.risk: Valve may be old/worn despite claim.
risks.proof: Close-up photo showing valve brand/date stamp or receipt for valve replacement.

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the stamped capacity and manufacture/test date on the cylinder collar.
Video of a soap-bubble or gauge-based leak test with valve open.
Photo of any safety certification sticker or inspection document.
Close-up of the valve showing any date/brand stamp to support 'new valve' claim.
response.reason: A verbal reassurance with no accompanying photo or document does not change the evidentiary basis; all claims remain unverified or unverifiable_remote, so the cylinder is still priced at worst case as untested, uncertified stock of unconfirmed capacity.
